1.mascotDialogue: Right, pay attention. Every node here knows precisely one thing about its neighbour: where the next one lives. That's it. Lose that pointer and everything downstream simply ceases to exist. Off we go — let's see it in C.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 3, and only line 3, matters. `next` is a pointer to another Node, not a value. `createNode` sets it to NULL first, every time — a new node doesn't presume to know what comes after it. Sensible of it.

3.mascotDialogue: Hover any line on the left and watch which node lights up on the right. `head->next->next` is just following the arrow twice. It really is that unremarkable.

4.mascotDialogue: Do look at node 2's arrow — pointing at nothing whatsoever. That's not the rendering lying to you, that's the honest state of the pointer. The code simply never told it to go anywhere else.
